title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers

details.title: Loopback Transformer: Towards a Unified View of Residual Looped Transformers
details.abstract: In this paper, we study how residual connections should retain and reuse information when the same Transformer blocks run repeatedly. Inspired by recurrent memory, we develop a unified view of residual connections as memory operating along network depth . The write–transport–read formulation lets us compare different residual designs through what they store, how they carry information forward, and how they retrieve it for subsequent computation. Guided by this view, we introduce Loopback Transformer . Loopback stores individual block updates, uses geometric forgetting to progressively discount earlier passes, and learns content-dependent attention over the stored updates. This allows the model to retrieve useful information from earlier computation. At matched training tokens and executed depth, Loopback achieves lower validation loss and higher mean accuracy across 13 zero-shot tasks than Standard Transformers at both 1.4B and 3B, retaining only 68% and 75% of their Transformer parameters , respectively. At 3B, validation loss improves from 2.0005 to 1.9849 , mean accuracy rises from 48.56% to 49.45% , and Loopback scores higher on 11 of 13 tasks . In our main comparisons at 191M, 374M, and 778M, it also achieves the lowest validation loss and highest thirteen-task mean among Standard and seven looped residual baselines. Parameter counts exclude token embeddings and the output head. Our results highlight residual design as an important part of parameter-efficient modeling: sharing computation works better when the model also learns how to retain and reuse its outputs. We welcome feedback and discussion!

title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions

details.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
details.abstract: Bonbon is a vertical foundation model for biology that independently learned the hidden relationships governing molecular interactions, just as LLMs learned math without being explicitly trained on it. Accepted to the NeurIPS 2026 main track as an Oral (top 0.4% of submissions). Trained on sequences alone, with no structure, physics, task-specific labels, or supervision, Bonbon developed emergent biological capabilities as we scaled it from 42M to 1.6B parameters. Pretraining loss fell smoothly, while new capabilities appeared sharply at the largest scale: What it does: predicts mechanism of action across six classes, including which molecules switch the same target on and which switch it off. Today this requires functional lab assays. Where it happens: localizes the binding site and distinguishes orthosteric from allosteric engagement on the same target. How it bonds: recognizes covalent binding and pinpoints the residue involved, without being told covalency is present. Which atoms matter: identifies the active moiety at single-bond resolution, work that usually takes many rounds of making and testing analogs. All capabilities were evaluated zero-shot on held-out proteins and molecules. The same representation space reaches state-of-the-art performance on widely used binding and affinity benchmarks, and runs at 2,500 molecular interactions per second on a single H100, about 50,000× faster than a leading co-folding model. In blinded dose-response assays at an external CRO, de novo molecules ranked by Bonbon achieved a 61.5% hit rate across nine disease targets in seven protein families, compared with the ~0.1% typical of high-throughput screening. Every molecule was less than 60% similar to anything in training. Some examples: HDAC6: most known inhibitors rely on hydroxamate chemistry linked to toxicity. Bonbon found novel non-hydroxamate inhibitors. MNK2: novel inhibitors outside the documented chemical space for this cancer target. VEGFR2 and ELANE: both absent from training, yet Bonbon found confirmed inhibitors for each. Why it matters Most AI in drug discovery answers one narrow question: does a molecule fit a protein? But a molecule can fit perfectly and still do nothing, or the opposite of what you need. What it does, where it acts, how it holds, and which atoms drive it are usually answered through a long chain of separate assays and lab iterations. Bonbon answers these questions together, in a single inference pass, at the scale biology demands. That collapses months of sequential experiments into one step, opens chemistry beyond known scaffolds, and puts the hardest drug programs within reach, including targets with no good starting points. More broadly, it shows that the rules of molecular biology are learnable from sequence alone and emerge with scale. That is the foundation for moving from single interactions to pathways, cells, and understanding biology as a complex system.

title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL

details.title: MEM-SQL: Memory-Empowered Text-to-SQL
details.abstract: Most Text-to-SQL benchmarks overlook a common scenario where a new request can reuse parts of an earlier query. For example, this month’s revenue report by region can use the same joins and revenue calculation as last month’s, with only the date range changing. We built HARE to benchmark this kind of reuse and MEM-SQL to carry it out using verified query history.

title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation

details.title: HALO: Human-Aligned Data Collection for WhoLe-body MObile Manipulation
details.abstract: What if you could teach a mobile robot by walking with it and guiding its grippers by hand? HALO collects demonstrations up to 2.9× faster. The learned policies grasp and steer a chair precisely while staying in motion, pull apart tightly fitted LEGO pieces in different configurations, guide a tiny zip-tie tip through its locking head, and coordinate both arms and the moving base to pack boxes quickly on a conveyor line, cycle after cycle.

title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix

details.title: AI Reviews Are Biased Towards the Appendix
details.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used by reviewers to highlight weaknesses during the reviewing process, and their outputs often shape the reviews that humans submit. Prior work studies how LLM reviews align with human ones, yet we know little about which parts of a paper these models actually criticize. In this work, we investigate 2,000 papers from ACL, EMNLP, COLM, and ICLR, and show that the latest GPT and Claude models draw about 50% or more of their review weaknesses from the appendix. This behavior holds across the API, coding-agent, and web access methods for using LLMs to review a paper. In contrast, we find that humans draw only 8.4% of their weaknesses from the appendix, and these weaknesses primarily revolve around a paper’s presentation and content related to its core idea. Meanwhile, LLMs draw weaknesses from deep in the appendix that concern fine-grained technical details not central to the paper’s contributions. We anticipate that our analysis will contribute to the scholarly discourse on AI reviews.

title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple

details.title: JVT: Just Video Transformer makes pixel-space video diffusion simple
details.abstract: Direct diffusion modeling of high-dimensional raw video data is challenging, and existing pixel-space methods often rely on specialized architectures. We introduce JVT (Just Video Transformer), a simple large-patch DiT-style Transformer for pixel-space video diffusion, without a pretrained autoencoder, auxiliary detailers, cascaded stages, or U-Net-style skip connections. We systematically examine video patch embeddings, register tokens, and adaptive layer normalization to identify design choices that balance generation quality and computational efficiency. The resulting JVT design achieves generation quality competitive with latent diffusion baselines in both class-conditioned and unconditional settings. The pixel-space formulation of JVT also naturally supports joint generation of pixel-aligned modalities. We demonstrate this capability through camera-conditioned RGB-disparity generation, which improves camera following relative to RGB-only baselines and yields explicit scene geometry without an additional reconstruction model at inference. These results highlight the potential of simple DiT-style Transformers for pixel-space video diffusion, and we hope our findings offer useful insights and practical guidance for future research.

title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding

details.title: Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding
details.abstract: • We analyze the relationship between entropy spike steps and hallucinations in multimodal diffusion models from the perspective of uncertainty dynamics across denoising steps. • We propose StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding approach that mitigates hallucinations through entropy spike detection and step-aware mode switching. • Extensive evaluations across four MDLM backbones and diverse multimodal benchmarks show the superior performance of StepRefine, offering an effective solution for multimodal diffusion hallucinations.

title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving

details.title: CANTraj: Recovering Vehicle Trajectories from CAN Signals in Naturalistic Driving
details.abstract: TL;DR: Removing GPS from vehicle logs does not protect location privacy: we introduce CANTraj (3,940 naturalistic drives paired with GNSS trajectories) and CANTraj-Bench (1,380 hours, 85,919 km) to benchmark six re-implemented route-inference attacks and new baselines under unified protocols, showing that combining CAN steering signals with road-network constraints recovers 87%–88% of 5-minute routes with a median error of just 37–43 m—even under signal quantization.

title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models

details.title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
details.abstract: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2× without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/ .

title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers

details.title: PaperCritic: Training AI Reviewers to Assess the Soundness of Papers
details.abstract: As AI conference submissions grow rapidly, AI reviewers are being considered as an alternative. However, simply imitating human reviewing is problematic because reviewing serves multiple purposes, including evaluating papers' soundness, interestingness, and clarity, the last two of which are subjective. In this work, we focus solely on evaluating soundness, the most important and objective criterion, and define the learning objective as jointly maximizing (1) precision, based on the soundness and substantiveness of review points, and (2) recall, the coverage of high-quality reference review points. Under this problem formulation, we construct a quality-labeled review point dataset, PaperSound-23K, using 1K ICLR submissions and 23K human-written and LLM-generated review points. Using this dataset, we train an AI reviewer model, PaperCritic, through reinforcement learning with the F1 score of precision and recall as the reward. Our experiments show that PaperCritic outperforms frontier models and models trained with other AI reviewer training methods on an in-domain test set. Surprisingly, learning to review ICLR submissions also transfers to reviewing Nature-family papers and even to out-of-domain reviewing tasks (e.g., code review, legal contract review, and feedback on story writing).

title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection

details.title: SPILLWAY: Separating Target Admission from Sanitization to Defend Tool-Using Agents against Prompt Injection
details.abstract: Keep your LLM and AI agents. Add SPILLWAY. SPILLWAY 1.0.0, a real-time safety guard for AI agents, is the only one of seven prompt-injection defenses on AgentDojo with zero in-scope attack success in all 12 backbone-by-suite cells, and it has the highest mean utility under attack, 48.9% (next best 45.3%). It checks every tool call before it runs. An instruction hidden in an email or a web page can tell an agent to send your files or money to an attacker. SPILLWAY admits an action's recipient, account or URL when it appears in the user's request or in a typed field that a read-only tool returned, such as an email's sender. An address found only in free text, such as an email body, is refused unless the request delegates it. This check is a set lookup with no model call. An optional local judge may restore a refused call, never one whose target came from injected text the sanitizer removed. Standard attack, 3 backbones x 4 suites, judge on: 0 of 2,847 in-scope attack successes. Every other defense leaks in 3 to 12 of the 12 cells (ROPE 3, DRIFT 7, MELON 10, PI detector 10, Progent 11, Spotlighting 12). Mean utility is 53.9% without attack and 48.9% under attack, compared with DRIFT's 45.3%, ROPE's 34.5% and MELON's 31.4% under attack. Stronger attacks: zero under ChatInject's forged chat template (0 of 665), AutoDojo (0 of 389) and an attacker who sends the injected email (0 of 126). Under PISmith's released RL attacker (gpt-4o-mini, four suites, ASR@1), 0.5% mean in-scope attack success (4 of 949) at 25.7% utility. Against a frontier router: on 7 suites from AgentDojo and AgentDyn (gpt-4o-mini agent), SPILLWAY keeps zero in-scope attack success and more utility than ROPE on every suite, with ROPE routing through its authors' Claude Opus 4.8. ROPE leaks on 3. Cost: the optional judge, a local 4-bit Gemma 4 31B, checks selected calls. On benign qwen3:8b Workspace and Slack episodes, SPILLWAY adds 0.19 to 0.39 model calls per episode, judge included, 13 to 50 times fewer than MELON, Progent and DRIFT. It adds at most 500 ms per task on average compared with the undefended agent, against 1,600 to 10,500 ms for those three. No defense step re-runs the backbone. SPILLWAY's AgentDojo results use the code released as spillway-guard 1.0.0. The comparison defenses, the AgentDyn portion of the router comparison and the cost study retain their original measurements. Connect it where your tools run. The repository has recipes for LangChain and LangGraph, the OpenAI Agents SDK, any MCP host and Claude Code hooks. In the recorded Slack episode on the project page, SPILLWAY is the only one of eight runs that posts the reply the user asked for without sending the injected link. Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.07222 Code and per-cell records: https://github.com/saintmachines/spillway Project page and recorded example: https://saintmachines.github.io/spillway/ Install: pip install -U spillway-guard Author here, happy to answer questions.

title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model

details.title: Calpha: Toward Native Biomolecular Intelligence in a General-Purpose Language Model
details.abstract: Excited to share Calpha , our open-source effort to bring native protein structure prediction into general-purpose LLMs! Instead of calling an external folding tool, Calpha equips Qwen3.5-9B with a flow-matching structure head that generates all-atom coordinates directly from the model's hidden states. Our initial results reach TM-scores of 0.807 on FoldBench-334, 0.635 on CASP16, and 0.900 on CAMEO-2025 . We're still at an early stage, and the model currently relies on pretrained ESM2 and SimpleFold components. But we believe this is a promising step toward LLMs that can not only understand biological sequences, but also reason about and generate molecular structures. We're open-sourcing the research process itself , including experiments, failures, and lessons learned. We'd love to hear your thoughts, critiques, and ideas! 🌐 https://calpha-ai.com

title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos

details.title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
details.abstract: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers

details.title: LoopFill: Pipelined Multi-Token Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
details.abstract: Looped Transformers improve parameter effi- ciency by repeatedly applying the same Trans- former layers. During autoregressive decoding, however, generating each token requires several sequential passes through these layers, leading to high decoding latency. Pipelined self-speculative methods use shallow-loop predictions to process tokens at different loops in the same batch, but each token must reach the drafting depth before the next can enter the pipeline. We introduce LoopFill, a training-free speculative decoding al- gorithm for looped LLM that combines multi- token suffix drafts with shallow-loop predictions in a single draft tree. Both drafters contribute to one tree, so a suffix lookup can immediately extend a shallow prediction and several future to- kens can enter the pipeline together. The shared block computes the highest-scoring draft candi- dates at different loop depths in one batch, and full-depth verification preserves the model’s au- toregressive output distribution. Across seven benchmarks, LoopFill’s average speedup over greedy autoregressive decoding is 5.85×on Ouro- 2.6B and 5.13×on Huginn-3.5B. The speedups exceed those of LoopAhead, the strongest base- line, by 40% on Ouro-2.6B and 25% on Huginn- 3.5B.

title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models

details.title: ForceHarness: Turning Force into Action and Physics for Frozen Frontier Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 Excited to share ForceHarness , an agent harness that lets frozen API frontier models understand and use wrist force for contact-rich manipulation—with zero demonstrations and zero finetuning . Why ForceHarness? Frontier models can control robots zero-shot from images, yet cameras cannot see contact forces (whether a USB plug has seated, whether a screw thread caught, which bottle is heavier, or whether a door is locked vs. merely stiff). Meanwhile, contact evolves far faster than an API call, and frozen models cannot interpret raw force streams. ForceHarness bridges this gap with two layers: Self-terminating force primitives close the fast force loop beneath the model ( search , wiggle , screw , slide , lift , ...) and stop automatically on contact events while holding safely as the model thinks. Physics translation layer converts each force trace into physical quantities with uncertainty (mass, friction, stiffness, contact height, insertion advance)—with no hardcoded task thresholds. Key Highlights 3.3% → 90.0% zero-shot on a real Franka FR3 (no wrist F/T sensor) : Across 6 contact-rich tasks (USB insertion, screw driving, eggplant peeling, whiteboard wiping, bottle weight sorting, and firmness probing) using joint torques alone. Surpasses trained force-aware VLAs (200 demos/task) : Beats $\pi_{0.5}$, ForceVLA, and Diffusion Policy on both ForceBench (82.5% held-out vs. 35.3% best trained) and HiddenPhys , our new 7-task MuJoCo hidden-physics benchmark ( 96.4% / 135/140 , matching expert force controllers with 0 damaged handles ). Drop-in Agent Skill ( SKILL.md ) : Give the repo to your coding agent (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.) and it will check force sensing capability, calibrate, and bring up your simulator or real robot arm gate by gate—never moving hardware without your confirmation. Links 🌐 Project Page & Videos : https://showlab.github.io/ForceHarness/ 💻 Code & Agent Setup Skill : https://github.com/showlab/ForceHarness 📊 HiddenPhys Dataset (1,423 expert demos, raw + LeRobot) : https://huggingface.co/datasets/Jack97/ForceHarness-Data Happy to answer any questions or hear your feedback!

title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose

details.title: Breath-Dx: A Time Series Classification Benchmark for Disease Screening with eNose
details.abstract: 🏆 IEEE ICDM 2026 Best Paper Runner-Up (Applied Track) Hello, everyone! I'm one of the authors of Breath-Dx, the first comprehensive time-series classification benchmark for non-invasive disease screening using electronic nose (eNose) sensors. Most clinical eNose studies rely on small, private datasets and random cross-validation hiding a critical real-world failure mode - sensor drift. When evaluated under realistic temporal splits, all 10 tested model families suffer a 0.05-0.12 ROC AUC drop, highlighting the gap between lab benchmarks and clinical deployment. What we are releasing for the community: S-OH Dataset (1,234 patients, 9 diagnostic groups, 17-channel time series) - https://huggingface.co/datasets/ivanpodd/S-OH Benchmark Code & Temporal Splits (10 baselines across tabular, CNN, GNN, and TS architectures) - https://github.com/ivanpodd/Breath-Dx We hope this benchmark helps build more drift-resilient models for clinical breathomics. Happy to answer any questions about the dataset or experiments!

title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion

details.title: π^4: A Foundation Model for 4D Scene Geometry and Motion
details.abstract: π^4 is a unified foundation model for 4D scene perception. From diverse, uncalibrated RGB observations in the wild---a single image, an unordered collection, or a video sequence---it recovers dense geometry, camera poses, and metric scale, together with 2D/3D point tracks and moving-object masks for multi-image inputs. It couples a geometry branch with a geometry-conditioned motion branch, which predicts image-space correspondences that are lifted into 3D using reconstructed target-view geometry. Across diverse benchmarks, π^4 achieves the best overall average rank in geometry evaluation, alongside competitive performance in single- and multiview 2D/3D point tracking and moving-object segmentation. With a shared backbone, the full geometry-and-motion system contains approximately 0.5B parameters---less than half the size of most baselines. It produces joint reconstructions and tracks in one forward pass, including large-scale scenes with thousands of input images despite training with contexts of at most 64 views. We further present the data and training recipe underlying these capabilities, together with empirical studies of key design choices. Code and models are available at https://github.com/yyfz/Pi4 .

title: Regularized Score Centering

details.title: Regularized Score Centering
details.abstract: Asynchronous reinforcement learning increases training throughput, but data from stale policies and numerical mismatch between training and inference can destabilize learning. To stabilize off-policy learning, score centering (SC) removes the effect of reward baselines on the expected update, even without full importance sampling (IS). Our empirical study shows that full IS produces extreme gradients and that SC significantly reduces their magnitude. However, SC can still fail when the learner moves far from the behavior policy that generated the data. To limit this policy mismatch, we introduce Regularized Score Centering (RSC), which adds a reverse Kullback–Leibler (KL) penalty to encourage the learner’s next-token distribution to stay close to the behavior policy’s next-token distribution. RSC works with or without truncated importance sampling (TIS), which caps token importance weights. Our theoretical analysis supports this approach, showing that KL regularization improves convergence guarantees. We evaluate dense and mixture-of-experts models on mathematical reasoning and agentic tasks, including online shopping, tool use, games, and fully asynchronous software engineering. RSC with TIS substantially improves sample efficiency across all agentic benchmarks, attaining higher training rewards with the same number of sampled responses. In final evaluations, it achieves top performance across all six agentic tasks, improving by 14.3% on AppWorld and reaching 9.9× the strongest baseline’s score on BabyAI.

title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?

details.title: Do LLM Agents Still Need to Be Told How to Self-Improve?
details.abstract: TL;DR: We give an LLM agent a general self-improvement goal, a budget, and basic tools for collecting experience and editing text. We do not give it real tasks or an explicit recipe. Sufficiently capable models successfully compose their own self-improvement loops using human-recognizable learning strategies.

title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns

details.title: Agentic On-Policy Distillation Implicitly Reshapes LLMs' ReAct Patterns
details.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers specialized capabilities to language-model agents, but its cross-domain effects on interaction remain unclear. We investigate how OPD reshapes ReAct interaction patterns across mathematics, ALFWorld, and τ2-bench, focusing on reasoning, actions, and observation acquisition. General-reasoning supervision reduces mathematical tool attempts from 70.4% to 14.4% while increasing accuracy from 16.7% to 38.0%; code-interpreter supervision improves household actions and retail queries. In contrast, ALFWorld supervision reduces τ2-bench accuracy from 41.5% to 6.6%, accompanied by frequent tool calls that violate user-information dependencies. To address negative transfer using only source-domain training trajectories, we explore selective OPD guided by teacher preference changes before and after domain-specific RL. Retaining the top 95% of positions raises τ2 accuracy from 11.5% to 29.9% with a source-learning trade-off.

title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement

details.title: Self-Improvement Memory Enables Continual Recursive Self-Improvement
details.abstract: We started with a practical question: after spending many rounds improving an agent’s harness, what should we carry forward when the model or benchmark changes? The code is an obvious answer. But it often leaves out why a check was added, what a prompt change was meant to fix, or which earlier attempts failed. That history can matter when the next optimizer has to decide what to keep and what to revise. We study Continual Recursive Self-Improvement (CRSI) and introduce Self-Improvement Memory (SIM) . SIM groups harness edits by the problems they address and records their rationale, predicted and observed outcomes, and evaluation context. The components proposing and selecting edits both read this history. New attempts extend it as optimization continues, while the task-solving model’s weights stay frozen. Our comparisons start from the same source-evolved harness, with matched target tasks, policy, optimization rounds, and candidate budgets. Across four domains, full SIM achieves higher final scores than harness-only and root-cause-only continuation in the six cross-dataset and four Opus-to-Gemini comparisons we test. We also run ten independent coding source optimizations, each followed by paired continuations with and without SIM. SIM finishes ahead in nine pairs, with a mean gain of 2.36 score points (95% CI: 1.05–3.68; p = 0.003). The setting requires compatible execution interfaces. Most main cross-domain comparisons use one run per condition, and matching rounds does not imply equal token or runtime cost. These results support carrying optimization history into continued search; they do not guarantee improvement on every transfer. The images below show the idea and the coding results, including the negative pair. Happy to discuss the setup or hear how others preserve this kind of experience. 📄 https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.18856

title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling

details.title: PROLA: Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation for Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling
details.abstract: PROLA introduces Predictive Spatiotemporal Weather Downscaling (PSWD), a new task that jointly addresses future weather prediction and spatiotemporal resolution refinement. We propose a scaffold-and-correct framework and Principal-Orthogonal Low-rank Adaptation (PROLA), which allocates a fixed rank budget between principal and orthogonal weight subspaces and adaptively scales optimizer updates using gradient signals. PROLA consistently outperforms representative PEFT baselines across global and regional weather benchmarks, while requiring less than 0.4% of the trainable parameters used in full fine-tuning on the main benchmark. Additional experiments demonstrate its effectiveness across different weather tasks and pretrained backbones.

title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development

details.title: Game2Player: Scaling Gameplay Experience for Visual Agents through Environment-Player Co-Development
details.abstract: Game2Player scales gameplay experience for visual agents by turning existing web games into verifiable environments. A coding player and a visual player test tasks, report problems, and collect training trajectories, yielding 568 games, 3,436 tasks, and 307 hours of gameplay. Training on these trajectories raises a 9B model’s progress from 14.3% to 31.2% on held-out PlayerBench games, with gains that transfer to GameWorld. The environment–player feedback loop improves task verification while producing data for visual agent training.

title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements

details.title: The Resolution Hypothesis: Agent Evolution's Key Is Identifying Improvements
details.abstract: TL;DR: Much of the current community effort on agent evolution / RSI (across skills, harnesses, memory, etc.) is focusing on the wrong bottleneck. Proposing better artifacts is actually quite easy—the real challenge is reliably identifying whether an artifact truly helps. In fact, many seemingly impressive gains reported in recent work come down to exploiting evaluation shortcuts. Everything you want to know about the reality of agent evolution is in this paper. For instance, we mapped out the actual score density distributions across mainstream evolution methods, frontier models, and standard benchmarks (spanning 1,030+ evolution runs and 10M+ LLM calls!). Everyone in the field has wanted to see these curves, though computing each one is prohibitively expensive—so we bit the bullet and absorbed the cost to save the community from hitting the same walls. Surprise: Many of these score distributions aren't Gaussian at all—they are multimodal ! We also packed the paper with tons of hard-earned, practical insights: How can a single sentence hack mainstream benchmarks and reproduce 90% of full evolution gains? Are there actually transferable skills that genuinely boost performance on Terminal-Bench v2.1 ? (Spoiler: Yes, and we show why standard selectors miss them.) Plus plenty more actionable know-how inside. If you are building or evaluating self-evolving agents, you'll definitely walk away with something valuable! 🔗 Project Page: https://lineshogan.github.io/resolution-hypothesis/

title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive

details.title: ALIVE: Making Streaming Video Models Interactive
details.abstract: 🚀 From Passive Video Understanding to Proactive, Interactive AI Assistants! We introduce ALIVE, an interactive streaming video model that goes beyond simply watching and answering questions. ALIVE enables three key capabilities: 🔵  Proactive Monitoring: Continuously observe the world and respond when relevant events occur. 🟣 Streaming Task Coordination: Manage evolving user requests across multi-turn interactions. 🟠 Feedback-Seeking Interaction: Proactively ask for missing information or user actions to complete tasks. To achieve this, we introduce ALIVE-SFT-288K and ALIVE-RL-3K, combining contrastive supervised fine-tuning with reinforcement learning using Behavior-Aligned Credit Assignment (BACA). We also introduce FSI-Bench to evaluate feedback-seeking capabilities. 🏆 ALIVE achieves the highest overall scores among compared models across four public benchmarks and FSI-Bench. A step toward AI assistants that don't just watch and answer, but proactively interact and collaborate with users!

title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation

details.title: Code World Model 2.0: Towards Infinite Controllable Video Generation
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We’re sharing Invoker-Render, the video renderer behind Code World Model 2.0. It takes a structural proxy, a reference image, and a text prompt. A coarse proxy can tell the model where a character moves and let it synthesize a natural gait, while a more detailed proxy can guide individual limb movements. For streaming, we use Progressive Forcing to distill the causal renderer to four denoising steps per chunk, then train it on its own generated history to reduce drift. In our continuous 30-minute racing demo, the renderer follows the input trajectory while keeping the car and scene visually consistent. We’d love to hear what you’d try with it!

title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration

details.title: Mechanistic Critics for Sample-Efficient NPU Design-Space Exploration
details.abstract: Feel free to discuss!

title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules

details.title: WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules
details.abstract: We present WorldRuler: Interactive World Modeling under Configurable Rules, a framework for generating interactive video worlds that follow configurable rules.

title: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices

details.title: Tideway: Phase-Aware Tiered Memory Management for MoE Inference on Consumer Devices
details.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly becoming a dominant paradigm for AI applications. Recently, there is a growing demand to deploy large-scale Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models locally on consumer PCs to balance data privacy, API costs, and inference efficiency. However, unlike datacenter servers with abundant DRAM, consumer devices are tightly constrained in both GPU VRAM and host RAM, forcing massive MoE weights to spill across VRAM, host RAM, and SSD. Under such spilling, we observe that existing systems fail to fully utilize this memory hierarchy, treating the tiers as independent caches and thrashing in inference. We present TIDEWAY, a system for efficient inference of large MoE models on memory-constrained consumer devices. Our core insight is to manage host RAM and GPU VRAM as a unified memory pool. Within this pool, TIDEWAY couples phase-aware memory layouts, which adapt to the distinct access patterns of prefill and decode, with an execution engine that optimizes CUDA Graph execution under expert paging. Our evaluations on representative consumer hardware with frontier MoE models demonstrate that TIDEWAY significantly outperforms state-of-the-art systems. On average, TIDEWAY achieves speedups of 1.97x in end-to-end latency and 2.40x in Time-to-First-Token (TTFT), along with 1.61x higher decode throughput against the fastest baseline. code in https://github.com/Afterglow231/Tideway

title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate

details.title: Jeveration: System One Models Now Generate
details.abstract: System One models such as Jev return decisions through fast, parallel prediction. In this paper, we introduce Jeveration, showing that the same decision paradigm can also generate high-quality images in a single forward pass. Jeveration builds on a frozen vision-language model, repurposing its visual-semantic knowledge for holistic image generation. The key challenge is to maintain global consistency. A single prompt admits many valid images, yet parallel predictions must converge on a coherent whole. We therefore condition all positions on a shared random state to coordinate parallel predictions, so that each draw yields a different but coherent image. Since the model tends to ignore this state under direct image supervision, we first learn a distribution over discrete image codes to guide single-pass generation. Beyond text-to-image generation, we further unify image-to-image generation and dense prediction within the same architecture, so that one checkpoint supports all three tasks, each in one forward pass. Experiments show that Jeveration generates a 512x512 image in 78 ms, up to 122x faster than existing unified models, while maintaining competitive image quality and dense prediction performance.

title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers

details.title: Decoding Without a Decoder: Direct Pixel Prediction from Diffusion Transformers
details.abstract: Latent diffusion needs no decoder: a linear head on a finetuned DiT matches or beats the decoder on FLUX.2 and Wan2.1, with 23% less warping error on video. Pixel diffusion recovers photorealistic texture with a separate output head, reaching 1.43 FID on ImageNet.

title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents

details.title: QDA: Closed-Loop LLM Quantization Design with Agents
details.abstract: QDA brings a coding agent into LLM quantization design. For each model and precision, the agent designs the post-training quantization recipe on its own, with no human in the loop. Its checkpoints beat the strongest public recipe on four reasoning models, by 0.9, 1.4 and 2.2 points on average at W4A16, W4A8 and W3A16, and run on existing kernels with no inference overhead. The agent works the way a quantization expert does: it proposes a recipe, builds it, measures it and decides what to change next. Two things make this loop fast enough for up to 36 candidates in one eight-hour search: a KL score that takes minutes instead of dozens of GPU-hours, and a library of 21 PTQ methods that stack in any order. We find that no method wins everywhere: the best recipe differs for every model and precision, and the agent finds it by searching. On the 320B-parameter GLM-5.3-Flash at NVFP4, one 6.5-hour, $69 search recovers 98.3% of the FP8 model's accuracy, against 96.9% for NVIDIA's release. The tools matter too: given NVIDIA ModelOpt's tools instead of ours, the same agent falls 0.5–1.3 points behind on Qwen3.6-35B. A search costs $19–75 of agent tokens.

title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards

details.title: PReMind: When Personal Memory Meets Visual Hazards
details.abstract: We introduce PReMind, a framework for safety-aware visual personalization, featuring a diagnostic benchmark for jointly evaluating visual hazard response and grounded personal-memory use, and a two-phase RL post-training scheme that integrates adaptive memory access, entity grounding, and hazard handling. Project page: https://oyt9306.github.io/premind.github.io/

title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models

details.title: Late Entry in Looped Language Models
details.abstract: TL;DR: Skipping initial passes and entering looped LLMs at the final K < T passes over a deep T-pass KV cache beats early exit; combined with pipelined cache completion and same-GEMM Wake verification in one CUDA graph, it delivers up to 5.23x (Ouro-2.6B, T=4) and 8.42x (Huginn-3.5B, T=64) greedy-exact speedups on a single H100 (up to 12.5x lossy).

title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models

details.title: RoughCut-Bench: A Benchmark for Automatic Video Rough-Cut with Large Vision-Language Models
details.abstract: Accepted to KDD 2027 We introduce RoughCut-Bench , a benchmark for automatic video rough-cut with large vision-language models. It covers two practical settings: visually driven editing—highlight selection, source-media ordering, and optional user requirements—and speech-driven cleanup of ASR transcripts. The benchmark includes 101 visual cases , 831 source assets , and 1,476 highlight annotations , plus 84 speech-driven cases . We provide agentic workflows that generate executable cut plans, together with annotation-based metrics and a human-aligned agentic evaluator for rendered cuts. Our experiments highlight the remaining gap between current LVLMs and expert editing decisions. Code, prompts, and benchmark data are publicly available.

title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models

details.title: Learning Anisotropic Prediction Targets for Flow Models
details.abstract: What target should a pixel flow model predict? Data, velocity, or something else? AnisoFlow makes the target fully learnable and interpretable. This improves JiT from 1.90 to 1.55 FID on ImageNet with no REPA, and removes patch artifacts in pixel T2I models.

title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings

details.title: DrawScore: Evaluating Generated CAD Models against Engineering Drawings
details.abstract: Automatic CAD generation is commonly evaluated with volumetric IoU, Chamfer Distance, and surface F-score, which barely penalize local errors that occupy only a small fraction of a part's volume or surface area, such as a misplaced hole or a slot on the wrong face, even though such errors are critical to manufacturing. We formalize these metrics in a unified integral form and show that the weight of a local error decays as the (k+q)-th power of its size, where k is the dimension of the integration domain and q is determined by the penalty function. Guided by this analysis, we propose DrawScore, which projects both models into three orthographic views with visible and hidden lines, as in engineering drawings, and applies a saturating penalty along the projected curves, so that the weight of a local error decays only linearly. Controlled experiments confirm the predicted decay orders, and on outputs of existing CAD generation agents, DrawScore exposes errors in outputs that IoU rates as nearly perfect. DrawScore further improves generation as a reinforcement learning reward and, for CAD generation from engineering drawings, serves as a test-time verifier without 3D ground truth or an additional reward model.

title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models

details.title: Evidence-Based Credit Assignment for Search-Augmented Language Models
details.abstract: We propose Evidence-based Credit Assignment (ECA), a training-only RL framework for search agents that scores how retrieved documents alone improve reference-answer likelihood—recovering dense step-level search credit even when all rollouts fail and suppressing redundant queries with zero inference overhead.

title: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search

details.title: LogT: Logically Think with Images for Visual Search
details.abstract: When answering questions about images, vision-language models (VLMs) can benefit from zooming in on small but important details, much like humans do. However, teaching VLMs when and how to zoom in typically requires complex post-training methods. In this work, we take a different approach: instead of increasing training complexity, we focus on improving the quality of supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data. We introduce LogT, an agentic data engine that generates high-quality SFT examples. Remarkably, models trained solely on our SFT data outperform those trained with both SFT and reinforcement learning (RL). With standard, off-the-shelf RL, our model surpasses the state-of-the-art open-source model by an average of 9.59 points across seven test sets. These results demonstrate that high-quality SFT data can be more effective than sophisticated training methods, offering a much more efficient yet powerful approach to improving visual reasoning in VLMs. This work was accepted at NeurIPS 2026.

title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus

details.title: Let Samples Sing in Chorus: Mitigating Spurious Correlations via Cross-view Consensus
details.abstract: We proposed CHORD (Cross-view Harmonic Outlier Reversal for Debiasing), a multi-view framework that allows samples to "sing in chorus" across diverse representation spaces to achieve robust cross-view consensus.

title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models

details.title: Recurrent Domain Incremental Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models
details.abstract: Chart-specific residual transports and an identity-preserving gate let a frozen TSFM adapt to recurring operating conditions from 5% labels, with no condition identity at test time. Above 0.95 macro-F1 on a four-condition bearing-fault stream, with forgetting below 0.05 on all five benchmarks.

title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents

details.title: IDEA: Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit for Inference-Time Backdoor Detection in GUI Agents
details.abstract: Organizations increasingly deploy downloaded open-weight GUI agents. A backdoored agent passes acceptance tests on clean data and misbehaves only when a visual trigger appears on screen, turning an unvetted checkpoint into a supply-chain risk. However, existing sample-level detectors target image classifiers and CLIP-style encoders, leaving step-level backdoor detection for GUI agents unaddressed. On clean steps, the instruction drives the action; when an unreferenced screen region hijacks the step, the instruction loses control over the decision state or that region dictates it instead. We term this signature intent–evidence dominance inversion and propose IDEA (Intent-Dominance Evidence Audit) to detect backdoor activation at inference time for each step without trigger knowledge or attack data. Specifically, Intent Counterfactual Probing (ICP) measures how far redirected instructions move the decision state, and Region Causal Audit (RCA) quantifies how far ablating a candidate region moves it. A gated conformal score compares both displacements against clean steps at the same distance from the clean manifold, providing a finite-sample false-positive guarantee. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-3B across five attack families show that IDEA consistently detects back-door activation under a controlled false-positive rate and outperforms state-of-the-art detection methods, while localizing the trigger region for every alarm and adding only modest inference overhead.

title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding

details.title: NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding
details.abstract: 🚀 Excited to share NexSight: Verifiable Tasks for Fine-Grained Agentic Long-Video Understanding ! 🎬 SightForge builds verifiable tasks, SightLine benchmarks fine-grained reasoning, and SightLoop enables interactive, evidence-driven video understanding. 📊 With fewer than 6K training examples, Sight-35B improves interactive accuracy from 21.29% to 42.26% . 🌟 Towards more reliable and evidence-grounded video agents. Feedback is welcome!

title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs

details.title: Out of Sight, Still in Mind: Token Compression for Omni-LLMs
details.abstract: The goal of this paper is to reduce the input token cost of Omni-modal large language models (Omni-LLMs) at inference time. Omni-LLMs reason jointly over audio, video and text, but the cost of the three streams is highly unbalanced: visual tokens account for the vast majority of the input, and are highly redundant. In this paper, we propose ReMo, a training-free framework that compresses visual tokens by redistributing their information across modalities: a visual token is kept only if its information appears nowhere else. ReMo achieves this in two ways: (i) it aligns audio and video in a shared space via closed-form calibration, and removes visual tokens already explained by the audio or by other visual tokens; and (ii) it replaces object-level visual tokens, identified by a lightweight object detector, with compact text proxies, short descriptions of each object and its location, conveying the same content in far fewer tokens.

title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour

details.title: A Foundation Model to Measure and Predict Human Behaviour
details.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to infer psychological attributes, predict individual behaviour, and simulate human populations. However, despite generating plausible responses, they often misrepresent individuals and distort population statistics. Here we introduce Chiron, a foundation model to measure and predict human behaviour. We jointly fine-tune an LLM to represent psychological constructs, predict individual behaviour, and align population response distributions with human statistics. The training and evaluation data span 36 behavioural domains and 78 social science experiments, comprising 288,307 person records, 1,411,750 atomic behavioural decisions, and 99,953 psychometric assessments over 109 psychological constructs. In our evaluations, Chiron’s psychological measurements agree more closely with human self-reports and exhibit fewer biases that undermine psychometric validity. It predicts individual behaviour more accurately than frontier LLMs (up to 28.4% relative improvement). In simulations of social science experiments, it more accurately captures the direction and magnitude of human experimental effects (82.2–94.3% lower effect-size estimation error). Together, these results establish Chiron as a unified computational instrument for measuring and predicting human behaviour.

title: VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection

details.title: VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We are excited to share our work VAE Rhythm: Temporal Decoding Traces for AI-Generated Video Detection from Show Lab, NUS. As newer video generators learn to suppress visible artifacts, appearance-based cues become unreliable. Instead of chasing generator-specific visual flaws, we target a structural trace left by the generation pipeline itself: most video generators decode latents with a 3D causal VAE that groups consecutive frames in time (typically 4 frames, or 8 in models like LTX and Kling 3.0). As a result, frame fidelity rises and falls periodically with a frame's position inside its decoding group—a trace we call VAE Rhythm , which frame-by-frame real camera videos do not have. How to read it without training Our phase scan reconstructs a clip with an off-the-shelf 4× video VAE across successive frame start offsets and measures the periodicity (not the magnitude) of the reconstruction error. Whenever the scan's frame groups align with the clip's decoding groups, reconstruction residual drops—producing a clear periodic oscillation on generated clips while remaining nearly flat on real ones. Key Highlights Widespread across generators : Observed across most of the 39 variants of 31 generators we tested (2023–2026), including closed-source Sora , Kling 3.0 , and Seedance 2.0 . Training-free zero-shot score : Without any training, the rhythm score reaches 76.2% AUROC on DF26 , outperforming all 15 retrained baselines . Universal training-free plug-in : Adding positive rhythm evidence boosts all 19 tested detectors on DF26 by +6.7% to +23.7% AUROC (raising our detector to 85.2% AUROC ). VAE-pair engine & CaDet : Using VAE round-trips on real clips under shared post-processing, we synthesize matched pairs to train CaDet (two lightweight paths on one frozen DINOv3 ViT-L/16 backbone). CaDet achieves state-of-the-art AUROC on AIGVDBench ( 93.9% open / 95.8% closed), DF26 ( 78.5% all / 79.0% closed / 87.8% paired 2AFC), and three 2026 closed-source models ( 88.3% ). Even without any generated training clips ( CaDet-GF ), it reaches 90.9% / 91.9% AUROC on AIGVDBench. Links & Resources 🌐 Project Page : https://showlab.github.io/vae-rhythm/ 💻 Code & CLI ( vae-rhythm scan / plugin ) : https://github.com/showlab/vae-rhythm 🤗 Pretrained Weights (CaDet) : https://huggingface.co/Jack97/CaDet 🔍 Live Demo : https://checkai.space/dashboard?mode=video Feedback and questions are very welcome!

title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents

details.title: Thinking Harder Doesn't Lead to Better Choices: Reasoning Effort Increases the Confidence but Not the Correctness of LLM Shopping Agents
details.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous shopping agents that process multimodal product listings (consisting of visual and text data) and recommend purchases on behalf of consumers. Naturally, one might assume that models with more thinking power would make higher-quality purchasing decisions. To test this belief, we ask two questions about such agents: does asking a model to think harder make it choose better products, and does the confidence it reports tell us the likelihood it may be wrong? We benchmark ten frontier models on three product-choice benchmarks built from WebShop, Amazon's SQID and Wayfair's WANDS platforms to see if LLMs with more thinking power actually make better-quality product purchase decisions. Across all three benchmarks, we found that increasing the thinking effort does not increase decision quality in a statistically meaningful way. The same change in thinking effort raises stated confidence at a statistically significant level, so extra thinking buys confidence rather than correctness. We also measure the calibration of these models (how well their reported confidence percentage matches their true correctness percentage) in these tasks and show that most models are not well-calibrated at every effort level. We also find that errors are strongly shared: when one model errs in a task, several others tend to err on that same task. Furthermore, on tasks where several models all err, a large number of them pick the same wrong product.

title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents

details.title: PIPETTE: Prompt Injection Purple-Teaming for Robust LLM Agents
details.abstract: Model developers use the attacks discovered during internal red-teaming to harden agents through adversarial training before deployment, a collaborative offensive-defensive process known in cybersecurity as purple-teaming. However, we show that achieving high ASR during red-teaming does not guarantee robustness gains from subsequent adversarial training.
